summary:
PyroSync is a multi-decadal Earth observation and fire intelligence platform that synchronizes over 25 years of NASA MODIS (1 km, 2000–present) and VIIRS (375 m, 2012–present) active-fire records across 9 Eastern Mediterranean countries into one deduplicated, scientifically traceable timeline.

When raw MODIS and VIIRS datasets are combined directly, two major distortions occur: (1) an artificial surge in fire counts after 2012 because VIIRS resolves ~7× smaller pixels than MODIS, and (2) same-day double-counting of the same wildfire across multiple satellites. Additionally, during extreme megafires, VIIRS 375 m thermal channels saturate at 367 K or fold over at 208 K, causing standard systems to severely underestimate the most dangerous fires.

PyroSync solves this end-to-end through a Footprint-Adaptive Medallion Data Pipeline, a 3-Model LightGBM Physics-Aware AI Ensemble (cutting fire radiative power prediction error by 31%), a 4-layer Clean Architecture FastAPI backend, and an interactive 3D Globe web platform with role-based views for Emergency Responders, Climate Scientists, and Land Managers.
details:
What PyroSync Does?

PyroSync unifies 2.55M+ raw NASA FIRMS detections across 9 Eastern Mediterranean countries (Greece, Turkey, Syria, Cyprus, Egypt, Lebanon, Israel, Jordan, and Palestine) from 2000 to 2026 into a single, reconciled 1 km / UTC-day analytical record—without discarding original NASA source IDs or falsifying pre-2012 VIIRS coverage gaps as zero.

How It Works (4 Integrated Subsystems)

1. Medallion ETL & Spatial Harmonization Pipeline:
  • Ingests 432 yearly MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS S-NPP 375 m files with SHA-256 provenance tracking, removes ~600k static gas-flare/industrial rows, converts timestamps to local solar dates, and quarantines invalid rows.
  • Uses KD-tree spatial-temporal matching (`match-1.1.0`) within ±60 minutes and each detection's true off-nadir satellite footprint (`scan × track`, 750 m–5 km), pairing 91,987 MODIS–VIIRS detections (median 598 m and 21 min apart).
  • Validated by 42 automated `pytest` checks (42 passed) and cross-sensor reconciliation audits.
2. Physics-Aware AI & Machine Learning Suite:
  • Model 1 (HOW STRONG — LightGBM 3-Model Blend): Trained on 1,405,427 VIIRS detections across 55 engineered physical and overpass-cluster features using a zero-leakage Stratified (Country × Date) Group Split (1.12M train / 141K val / 139K test). Blending Weighted Tweedie (50%), Log-L2 (30%), and Raw-L2 Tail Specialist (20%) recovers true Fire Radiative Power (MW) even when VIIRS I4 saturates at 367 K or folds over at 208 K—reducing test RMSE by 30.9% (13.90 → 9.60 MW, R²_log = 0.817).
  • Model 2 (WHEN — Anomaly Intelligence): Compares each week and month against the same seasonal window across the 2012–2023 baseline using Median % Change and MAD-based robust z-scores (Normal → Elevated → Extreme).
  • Model 3 (WHAT KIND & WHERE — Fire-Regime Patterns): Uses spatial DBSCAN clustering and thermal persistence signatures to separate destructive high-intensity forest wildfires from routine small-scale agricultural crop burns.
3. 4-Layer Clean Architecture Backend :
  • Built with Python FastAPI and Uvicorn in strict Domain / Application / Infrastructure / Presentation layers, serving Gold JSON/Parquet datasets, SQL schema metadata, streaming CSV exports, and real-time `<30 ms` ML inference via `GET /api/predict-frp`.
4. Interactive 3D Web Platform:
  • Built with React 19, TypeScript, Vite, and Three.js.
  • Features 3 Role-Based Intelligence Views (Emergency Responder, Climate Scientist, Land Manager), a 3D Globe & 2D Map with bounding-box filtering, an interactive 4-step Harmonization Grid, a 0°–55° Pixel Footprint Explorer, a 26-year Thermal History Matrix, a Live AI FRP Intensity Predictor, and a scientific CSV + Dataset Provenance Brief exporter.

Key Benefits & Impact

  • Prevents false post-2012 climate trend conclusions caused by multi-sensor resolution gaps.
  • Ensures emergency responders never underestimate extreme megafires due to sensor saturation.
  • Helps land managers direct firefighting aircraft and budgets to high-intensity wildfires rather than routine agricultural burning.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Languages: Python 3.11+, TypeScript, SQL
  • Data & ML: Pandas, PyArrow, NumPy, SciPy (KD-Tree), LightGBM, Scikit-learn, Joblib, Pytest
  • Backend: FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic/Dataclasses
  • Frontend: React 19, Vite, Three.js, HTML5/CSS3, Node Test Runner

Source Code: https://github.com/abdobakr5/PyroSync
